name: Contraposition (P→Q ⊢ ¬Q→¬P)
description: Contraposition in Existential Graphs — and the EG insight that it is almost free: P→Q and ¬Q→¬P are the *same graph* up to a double cut, both ¬(P∧¬Q). Starting from the scroll ~[ (P) ~[(Q)] ], one DC+ around P yields ~[ ~[~[(P)]] ~[(Q)] ], which reads as the scroll 'if ¬Q then ¬P'. The contrapositive isn't derived so much as read off the same picture — a vivid case of the diagram being the proposition.
